question.worked_solution:
If $X$ is a discrete random variable with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S,$ the expected value of ${X}^{2}$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[{X}^{2}]={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each squared value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}{x}^{2}\cdot f(x) \\  & ={0}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{10}+{1}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{5}+{2}^{2}\cdot \frac{2}{5}+{3}^{2}\cdot 0+{4}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{10}+{5}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{5}+{6}^{2}\cdot 0 \\  & =0\cdot \frac{1}{10}+1\cdot \frac{1}{5}+4\cdot \frac{2}{5}+9\cdot 0+16\cdot \frac{1}{10}+25\cdot \frac{1}{5}+36\cdot 0 \\  & =\frac{42}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
